case.background: Monochromatic light illuminates a clean cathode in a vacuum phototube. Vary frequency and intensity, then use stopping potential and saturation current to explain when and how electrons are emitted.
initial_observations: Some illumination settings produce no measurable photocurrent.
When electrons are emitted, a reverse voltage can stop the current.

controls.description: Intensity relative to the reference beam.
controls.name: intensity_relative

instruments.description: A clean-cathode vacuum phototube with monochromatic illumination and electrical meters.
instruments.name: vacuum_phototube

notes: The cathode remains clean and unchanged across experiments.
Zero current and stopping potential mean no emitted electrons.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: stopping_potential_v, saturation_current_ua. EXPR is the shared family-neutral JSON arithmetic tree over public controls. Supported operators are: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, log, sin, maximum, step. No candidate law family or truth-specific parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Potential needed to reduce photocurrent to zero.
readouts.name: stopping_potential_v

readouts.description: Saturation photocurrent under the chosen illumination.
readouts.name: saturation_current_ua

case.title: Discover the phototube frequency-intensity response
